reason: Yahweh is explicitly depicted as the national God of Israel/the Hebrews throughout this text. The passage repeatedly identifies Him as 'אֱלֹהֵי הָעִבְרִים' (Elohei ha-Ivrim - 'God of the Hebrews'), refers to Israel as 'עַמִּי' (ammi - 'my people'), and demonstrates His exclusive concern and preferential treatment for the Israelite nation over Egypt. Key examples include: (1) the stated purpose of liberation 'for my people,' (2) the explicit divine distinction 'בֵּין מִקְנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבֵין מִקְנֵה מִצְרָיִם' (between the livestock of Israel and Egypt), (3) the protection of Israelite territory 'רַק בְּאֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן...לֹא הָיָה בָּרָד' (only in the land of Goshen...there was no hail), and (4) the overarching narrative of divine action on behalf of one specific nation against another.
